history.new: Knuth 1988; Arnoux 1989; all shifts s >= 2 and the failures at s = 0, 1 are in A. Messaoudi, Math. Slovaca 50 (2000), Thm 6 and Prop 1 (Historian audit 2026-10-18, reviews/historian_C03_C10.md). The Lean proof is a verification asset.
history.old: t = 0 is Knuth (Appl. Math. Lett. 1, 1988) with Arnoux's Z[phi] proof (Appl. Math. Lett. 2, 1989); the shift extension follows from the same window and is covered by the "sufficiently large parameter" theorem of Grabner-Petho-Tichy-Woeginger (1994).

novelty_basis: Knuth 1988; Arnoux 1989; all shifts s >= 2 and the failures at s = 0, 1 are in A. Messaoudi, Math. Slovaca 50 (2000), Thm 6 and Prop 1 (Historian audit 2026-10-18, reviews/historian_C03_C10.md). The Lean proof is a verification asset.
proof_check: Lean 4 + Mathlib (Infinity.C08.circ_assoc, circ_comm, key, window; standard axioms only) for all t >= 0; counterexamples for s = 0, 1 by computation; no failure in 20,000 random triples up to 1e9 (t = 0)
statement:
For every t >= 0 the operation a o_t b = sum_{k in Z(a)} sum_{l in Z(b)} F_(k+l+t) on the natural numbers
(Z(n) the Zeckendorf index set, indices >= 2) is associative and commutative; in the lab's G-indexing these
are the shifts s = t + 2 >= 2. For s = 0 and s = 1 associativity fails ((2 o 4) o 4 != 2 o (4 o 4) for s = 0,
(1 o 4) o 4 != 1 o (4 o 4) for s = 1).
title: Every shifted Knuth product a o_t b = sum F(k+l+t) over Zeckendorf indices is associative (t >= 0)
